title: security-eng-sync-notes-2026-03-13
summary: Weekly security eng sync focused on vuln triage for recent dependency findings, secrets scanning false positives, threat modelling for rollout service, and next steps for remediation and monitoring.
content:
Attendees: Elena Park (owner), Marco Alvarez, Priya Shah, Daniel Kim, Sophie Nguyen, Rahul Desai (SRE), guest: Tom Becker (serving-runtime)

Agenda:
- Quick status updates (30m)
- Vulnerability triage: dependency scanner results from last week (45m)
- Secrets scanning: follow-ups and false positive review (20m)
- Threat modeling: rollout policy/automatic fallback (30m)
- Action items and owners (10m)

Notes:
1) Quick status
- Sprint context: most infra teams are in a code freeze window for the Dedicated rollout; security reviews need to be non-blocking but thorough.
- Metrics: scanning pipeline ran on 2026-03-12 across main repos. 12 new findings flagged, 3 classified as high/critical pending triage.

2) Vulnerability triage (detailed)
- JIRA-SEC-4823: critical CVE in postgres-driver 2.4.1 -> CVE-2026-1462 (deserialization vulnerability).
  - Affected repos: private-deployments (vpc-agent), platform-engineering (db-migration-worker).
  - Exploitability: medium-high — requires network access to DB port; however in private deployments customers may expose DB over private networks. Risk: data exfiltration and arbitrary code execution in worker.
  - Immediate mitigation: upgrade to postgres-driver 2.4.3 which contains patch. Priya to open PRs in both repos and request expedited review. ETA: 2026-03-15.
  - Short-term mitigation: add WAF rule to block unexpected proto/serialized payloads for migration endpoints (SRE: Rahul). ETA: 2026-03-14.
  - Post-mitigation verification: run dependency scanner and integration tests, confirm no regressions. Owner: Priya.

- JIRA-SEC-4815: high severity RCE vector in third-party image-processing lib (imgprocjs 0.9.8)
  - Affected: console-and-rollouts (thumbnail service used by console previews).
  - Current status: upstream patch available 0.9.10 but introduces minor API change that breaks existing tests.
  - Decision: create adapter shim in thumbnail service rather than pinning to older vulnerable version long-term. Marco to prototype shim; spike to be completed by 2026-03-18. Mark as planned mitigations.
  - Rollout plan: canary update for console-prod preview tenants, monitor errors for 48 hours, automatic rollback on >1% error rate.

- Misc medium findings (summary): 9 packages (devDeps mostly) with medium severity; flagged for normal patch cadence. Team to prioritise packages used in production runtimes first.

3) Secrets scanning
- Weekly scan results: 5 new potential secrets flagged across repos. After review by Sophie and Daniel, 3 were confirmed false positives (test fixtures, encoded tokens used for mock infra). Two were valid:
  - keys found in analytics-instrumentation repo: API key for legacy analytics vendor. Owner: product-ops. Action: rotate key, add to vault, remove from repo. Sophie to coordinate rotation. ETA: 2026-03-14.
  - AWS key in solutions-engineering-and-professional-services (accidental commit by consultant): Immediately rotated by infra team; incident ticket opened and consultant access revoked. Follow-up: run org-wide git-secrets pre-commit enforcement for all repos receiving external contributions. Owner: Daniel. ETA: 2026-03-20.
- False positives: note to update scanning rules to ignore test fixture pattern and encoded jwt-like strings used by e2e harness. Sophie to raise rule change PR. ETA: 2026-03-16.

4) Threat modeling: rollout policy and automatic fallback
- Context: Product team is rolling out new automatic model fallback feature (route to cheaper model variant on high load). This impacts smart routing and Dedicated/private behaviors.
- Threat surface considered:
  - Integrity risk: attacker may attempt to manipulate routing metadata to force downgrade to unconstrained/less-accurate model version causing data leakage or wrong outputs.
  - Availability risk: fallback could be exploited to create hot paths that starve capacity for other customers.
  - Confidentiality: routing decisions contain customer metadata; ensure PII isn't leaked into logs or externals when fallback triggers.
- Findings & mitigations:
  - Authenticate and sign routing tokens. Design decision: use mTLS plus HMAC-signed routing tokens between control plane and runtime. Owner: Tom (serving-runtime) + Platform engineering. ETA: design doc 2026-03-20 (linked in artifacts).
  - Rate-limit fallbacks per tenant and implement per-tenant circuit-breaker. Rahul to add policy to SRE autoscaler layer. ETA: 2026-03-25.
  - Logging: scrub routing metadata; maintain mapping only in secure, access-controlled observability pipeline (no raw tenant metadata forwarded to external metrics). Sophie to update logging guidelines. ETA: 2026-03-19.
  - Threat modeling follow-up: schedule focused threat model session with product and infra next week - targeted attendees: product-hosted-api, platform-engineering, eng-serving-runtime, security. Owner: Elena. Meeting: 2026-03-17 10:00am PT.

5) Incident response / exercises
- Tabletop exercise planned for simulated secrets leak in private deployment. Goals: test rotation runbook, customer communications, and on-prem recovery steps. Daniel to draft exercise plan. ETA: 2026-03-22.

6) Tooling & pipeline improvements
- Dependency scanner: reduce noise by applying low-signal suppression for dev-only deps. Priya to update scanner config and validate. ETA: 2026-03-16.
- Pre-merge gating: add automated SCA check to block merges for packages with critical fixes unless a security exemption is filed. Marco to propose gating rules. ETA: 2026-03-18.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Priya: open PRs to upgrade postgres-driver in vpc-agent and db-migration-worker; run tests and notify SRE. ETA 2026-03-15. (JIRA-SEC-4823)
- Rahul: add WAF rule and autoscaler circuit-breaker policy for fallbacks; short-term WAF rule by 2026-03-14; circuit-breaker by 2026-03-25.
- Marco: prototype adapter shim for imgprocjs upgrade; propose canary rollout plan. ETA 2026-03-18.
- Sophie: rotate analytics vendor key and update secrets scanning rules for test fixtures. ETA 2026-03-14 and 2026-03-16.
- Daniel: enforce git-secrets pre-commit for repos with external contributors; draft tabletop exercise plan. ETA 2026-03-20 and 2026-03-22.
- Tom: design doc for signed routing tokens (mTLS + HMAC) for fallback flow. ETA 2026-03-20.
- Elena: schedule threat-modeling deep-dive for rollout policy (2026-03-17) and follow-up notes.

Decisions made:
- Upgrade vulnerable postgres-driver immediately (no workaround).
- Use adapter shim approach for imgprocjs to avoid breaking console behavior while patching.
- Enforce stricter pre-merge gating for critical SCA findings.

Open questions / risks:
- Are there on-prem customers who expose DB ports in ways that make CVE-2026-1462 trivially exploitable? Ops to compile customer inventory. Owner: Rahul. ETA: 2026-03-16.
- How will fallback metrics surface in customer billing/console? Product to confirm impact; if billing differences exist, we must provide clear telemetry for audits.

Next sync: 2026-03-20 09:00am PT (tentative) — focus on progress for critical remediations and threat modeling outputs.

Attachments / links referenced:
- JIRA-SEC-4823 (postgres-driver CVE writeup)
- JIRA-SEC-4815 (imgprocjs RCE finding)
- github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/726 (initial shim spike)
- confluence.redwood/company/security/secrets-guidelines (secrets rotation runbook)

End of notes.
